key_insight: A learned convolution-based closure can predict atmospheric boundary-layer heat and momentum fluxes from mean profiles more accurately than a standard K-profile scheme while remaining physically interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to improve coarse-resolution weather and climate models with a transparent flux parameterization that is better suited for both unstable and stable boundary-layer conditions.
method: Train linearized convolution operators on nondimensional mean temperature and velocity profiles from high-resolution LES.
Test multiple first-order closure variants for heat and momentum flux prediction across stability regimes.
Select the best model by mean-squared error and assess it in a posteriori single-column simulations.
evidence_signal: The model was trained and evaluated on LES cases spanning multiple stability regimes and was also tested in single-column simulations, where it stayed stable and matched LES profiles closely.
watch_item: Because the closure is trained on idealized homogeneous-surface LES, performance may degrade in more heterogeneous or strongly non-ideal real-world boundary layers.
paper_title: Data-Driven Flux Parameterization for the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
